standard.title: Timetables and itineraries
standard.description: Interpret and use timetables and itineraries to plan activities and determine the duration of events and journeys
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can compare 12- and 24-hour time systems and solve conversion problems (AC9M5M03). They can read and interpret time in both 12- and 24-hour formats. They have not yet applied time reading skills to multi-row timetables or planned itineraries requiring calculation of durations across multiple legs.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students can interpret and use timetables and itineraries to plan activities and determine durations of events and journeys.

nodes.label: Reading timetables
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can read and extract information from a multi-row timetable, including departure and arrival times, duration, and frequency of services.
nodes.minimum_width: Read departure and arrival times from a provided timetable for at least three services; identify the duration of at least two journeys; identify the next available service after a given time.
nodes.typical_width: Extract a range of information from timetables in both 12- and 24-hour formats; calculate journey durations including those that cross the hour; read timetables with multiple routes or services; identify connections between services.
wider: Compare timetables across different transport types (bus, train, ferry) and identify how each is structured and what information each prioritises
Investigate how timetables are designed to be read quickly — what conventions make them usable, and what would make them confusing?
success_criteria: Student correctly reads departure and arrival times from a timetable.
Student calculates the duration of a journey from timetable information.

nodes.label: Calculating duration across time periods
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can calculate the duration of events and journeys, including those spanning hours, days, or involving 12-/24-hour format conversions.
nodes.minimum_width: Calculate the duration of at least four time intervals, including at least one that crosses midday or midnight; show working for each.
nodes.typical_width: Calculate durations using counting-on, subtraction, and number line strategies; convert between 12- and 24-hour format as needed for calculation; determine elapsed time in hours and minutes; apply to checking timetable information.
wider: Investigate duration calculations across time zones — if a flight leaves Sydney at 7:30 pm AEDT and lands in Tokyo 9 hours 45 minutes later, what is the Tokyo arrival time?
Explore historical calendars and timekeeping challenges — how were durations calculated before standardised time zones?

response_modes.reason: Duration calculation is error-prone at boundaries — crossing midday/midnight, dealing with non-decimal time (60 minutes in an hour). Fluency requires targeted practice with these boundary cases rather than routine whole-hour calculations.

nodes.hinge_reason: Reliable duration calculation at time boundaries (midday/midnight crossings) is the prerequisite for Node 3 itinerary planning. Students who make errors at boundaries will plan infeasible itineraries and cannot verify whether connection times are adequate.
success_criteria: Student correctly calculates the duration of a time interval, including one that crosses a time boundary (e.g. midday or midnight).
Student shows a strategy for the calculation.

nodes.label: Planning with itineraries
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can plan a multi-activity or multi-leg itinerary using timetables, calculating total durations, identifying constraints, and making decisions about timing.
nodes.minimum_width: Plan a simple two- or three-leg itinerary using a provided timetable; identify departure and arrival times for each leg; calculate total journey time.
nodes.typical_width: Plan a multi-leg itinerary accounting for connection times, waiting times, and constraints; identify the latest departure time for a given arrival deadline; determine whether a planned itinerary is feasible; communicate the plan as a clear schedule.
wider: Plan a real or realistic class excursion or event itinerary with multiple activities and constraints and present it as a formatted schedule
Investigate how airlines, event organisers, or schools build buffer time into schedules and discuss the trade-off between efficiency and reliability

response_modes.reason: Itinerary planning requires simultaneous management of timetable reading, duration calculation, and constraint satisfaction. The coordination of all three — while making decisions about feasibility and sequence — is the practical problem-solving goal of this standard.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Itinerary planning is an authentic, motivating application context. Real-world complexity — time zones, transport connections, event programs — provides genuinely broad terrain for advancing students.
success_criteria: Student constructs a feasible multi-leg itinerary from timetable information.
Student identifies the total duration of the planned journey or schedule.
